sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: MiniMind is an open-source project for training a tiny language model (about 64M parameters) completely from scratch on a personal GPU. It includes the full pipeline, from tokenizer and pretraining to fine-tuning, reinforcement learning and tool use, written in plain PyTorch.
sixtySeconds.problem: Libraries like transformers and trl hide how LLMs are actually built behind a few lines of code. MiniMind implements every stage itself so you can read, run and change it, and the README says a basic model can be trained in about 2 hours on one RTX 3090.
whoFor: Learners who want to understand LLM training end to end
Students with a single consumer GPU
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it as a hands-on, reproducible tutorial for building an LLM. The models are deliberately tiny, so they're for learning, not production use.
requirements: PyTorch, ideally with an NVIDIA GPU (CPU and MPS work but are slower)

overview: MiniMind provides a Dense and MoE model architecture aligned with the Qwen3 ecosystem, plus tokenizer training code. Training stages cover pretraining, supervised fine-tuning, LoRA, DPO, reinforcement learning from AI feedback (PPO, GRPO, CISPO), tool use, agentic RL, adaptive thinking and distillation, all implemented from scratch.

Datasets for every stage are published, and for a quick start you only need two small files to reproduce the MiniMind Zero chat model. Training supports single or multi-GPU (DDP, DeepSpeed), wandb or swanlab logging and resuming from checkpoints.

Trained models work with transformers, llama.cpp, vLLM and Ollama, and the project includes an OpenAI-compatible API server and a Streamlit chat web UI. The README's 2-hour and RMB 3 figures refer to one epoch of SFT on a single RTX 3090.

costs.label: Compute
costs.value: Your own GPU or rented GPU time; the README cites about RMB 3 for one SFT epoch on a rented 3090.

troubleshooting.solution: Check torch.cuda.is_available(); CPU and MPS work but are much slower.
Add --from_resume 1 to resume from the last checkpoint.

troubleshooting.problem: Web demo can't find the model
troubleshooting.solution: Copy the transformers-format model folder into ./scripts/ first, for example cp -r minimind-3 ./scripts/minimind-3.
